subject: Optimize Toolkit: pilot packaging & discount structure for CloudLedger
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@cloudledger.com>

Cc: Kate Reynolds <kate@cloudledger.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluate Optimize toolkit savings for our high-throughput ledger search

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput numbers looked promising. We
are trying to scope a 3-month pilot to justify the move from our current managed
API to a more cost-predictable dedicated flow. Key asks from procurement: a
clear credit or discount structure tied to batching and KV cache usage, and some
quantization guardrails (we can't degrade accuracy on reconciliation queries).

Can you send a concise packaging proposal that shows:
- pilot price (month-by-month) with commit bands
- expected per-token delta vs our current provider for typical ledger queries
- any constraints on model variants / quantization levels you would permit for
QA during pilot

Cc'ing Kate (SRE) to keep ops in the loop. Ideally we can keep the pilot
under a single PO and avoid bespoke legal terms if possible.

Best,
Samir

--
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudLedger
samir@cloudledger.com
+1 415-555-0134
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@cloudledger.com>
Cc: marucs_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Kate Reynolds <kate@cloudledger.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Mar 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluate Optimize toolkit savings for our high-throughput ledger search

Samir — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a short packaging sketch plus a
linked cost model we can walk through. Short summary up front:

1) Pilot structure (90 days)
   - Committed baseline: $25k / month (reserve for predictable throughput)
   - Consumption overlay: usage billed monthly with 15% pilot discount on token
     units beyond baseline
   - Ops credits: 100k inference credits (applied to prefix caching + warm-up)

2) Efficiency guarantees and tradeoffs
   - We recommend starting with the 16-bit quantized variant (q4_16 style) for
     non-reconciliation routes to capture ~35% reduced cost with <2% loss in
     intent-level accuracy.
   - Reconciliation queries (exact-match, high-precision) run on a 32-bit
     verified model; these will be routed with higher-cost profile but lower
     latency variability.

3) Batching & KV cache incentives
   - If prefix/KV cache hit rate exceeds 40% on production traffic, Redwood
     will provide an additional 10% rebate on consumption charges for the
     following month (measured on 95th-percentile traffic).
   - We include an automatic batching policy that keeps p99 latency under the
     SLO; you can opt into aggressive batching for background jobs for an
     additional 5% discount.

4) Exit & handoff
   - If you elect to stop after the pilot, we'll provide a final export of
     cached artifacts and a two-week ops runbook.

I'll let Marcus and Karthik add technical caveats (latency guardrails &
quantization notes). If that looks directionally right, we can send a one-page
MA and a PO-ready price appendix.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Attachments: CloudLedger_MA_proposal_v3.pdf, batching-cost-model.xlsx

Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit: pilot packaging & discount structure for CloudLedger

Samir / team — quick tech notes to make the pricing sketch actionable: 

1) Quantization recommendations (practical control):
   - Start with mixed-precision q4_0 for conversational/summary routes and
     q8_0 for reconciliation if you need deterministic float behavior. We
     rarely see >1.5% delta for semantic tasks with q4_0 at sequence lengths
     under 1024 tokens.

2) Batching & latency tradeoffs:
   - For interactive UI routes: target dynamic batching with max batch=16 and a
     microbatch timeout of 6ms to keep p95 latency below 180ms. That keeps UX
     snappy and still captures batched throughput gains.
   - For asynchronous reconciliation: allow a larger max batch (64+) and
     longer microbatch windows to maximize GPU occupancy; we can offer a
     separate discount for these background queues.

3) Measurement and SLOs:
   - We'll instrument token-level accounting and prefix cache hit-rate with
     per-route metrics. For the rebate you requested, hits will be computed
     daily and aggregated monthly (we'll share the raw logs for audit).

4) Attachments and quick checks:
   - See "quantization-recs.md" (attached) for per-model expected deltas on a
     small reconciliation prompt set you shared. I recommend you run the set
     against your golden data during the first two weeks of the pilot.

If the plan is accepted, ops and I will set up a short technical onboarding
call (30–45 min) to finalize routing policies and the caching keys you want
shared.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit: pilot packaging & discount structure for CloudLedger

Vanessa / Marcus — this looks pragmatic and close to what procurement will
approve. A few quick confirmations before I circulate to legal/finance: 

- The 15% pilot discount on consumption beyond baseline: is that applied to
  token costs only (yes) and is it stackable with the caching rebate?
- For the rebate, what is the exact measurement window and what happens if
  we oscillate around 40% (does partial month prorate)?
- Can you add in a short permitted-quantization clause (e.g. allow q4 for
  non-recon routes and require a signed exception for any replacement of
  verified 32-bit models)?

If you can answer the three items in a one-page appendix, we can route a
PO for the committed baseline next week and start onboarding the week after.

Thanks — Samir
